page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU instance featuring three dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 170 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate single-core capability paired with weaker multi-core scaling. The single-core Geekbench score of 1343.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1705.53 fall into the average tier, while the multi-core Geekbench score of 3293.0 and Passmark CPU score of 5574.75 are categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth shows a similar split, with large-block write speeds reaching an average of 26.33 GB/sec, whereas read bandwidth remains in the lower tier.

The fractional NVIDIA A16 GPU enables entry-level accelerated tasks. LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model show average performance, processing 549.08 tokens per second for prompts and generating 125.03 tokens per second. However, scaling to a medium 7B model results in poor performance, yielding 11.05 tokens per second for prompt processing and 4.56 tokens per second for text generation.

This instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads that do not require a full dedicated GPU or massive parallel CPU compute. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 10 GB per core makes it suitable for lightweight machine learning inference, small-scale data processing, and development environments. It is less suited for heavy multi-threaded CPU tasks, large-scale database operations, or high-throughput web serving due to lower multi-core and database benchmark scores.
description: The Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU instance designed for entry-level accelerated workloads. It features three dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a 170 GB NVMe SSD. Acceleration is delivered via a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data shows average single-core CPU performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1343.0, but weaker multi-core scaling. LLM inference on a small 135M model achieves average speeds of 125.03 tokens per second for text generation, though performance drops significantly on larger 7B models. This instance provides a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring moderate system memory and basic GPU acceleration, such as lightweight machine learning inference, model prototyping, and development environments, rather than heavy multi-threaded compute or large-scale database operations.
